chapter: Southwestern bands and New Orleans youth
title: Southwestern bands: Trent, Lazy Daddy and the Royal Garden Band
summary: Troy and Trent were the main big bands; Edgar Perry led the little-remembered Royal Garden Band.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: And who were some of the great Southwestern bands?

Well now there were quite a number of those bands and I just can't recall all of them. The two to the name were the outstanding ones, Troy and Trent. Of course in Galveston, Texas you had a band named Lazy Daddy's Band. Then you had the Royal Garden Band that left from Texas and went to California, which was another tremendous pioneer band. And Eddie Hewitt's daddy would come through there. He was a piano player. But there weren't too many big bands. Most of them concentrated on three, four and five piece combos.
What was the Royal Garden Band?
The Royal Garden was about seven or eight pieces.
Edgar Perry, a piano player. A tremendous piano player, Edgar Perry.

Well, the history behind him is kind of vague. I don't know of too many people that can recall Edgar Perry. Some of them in San Antonio do recall him and they remember him playing and leaving. The musicians that would know him would be like A.J. Johnson and he's past.
So there's just a band that disappeared from the scene. That's right. Maybe you could find something in California or something.
